title: harnessimo.config.json
description: Which checks this repository has asked the harness to enforce. A section left out is a check that does not run — `harnessimo doctor` reports it as not set rather than implying otherwise.

docs.description: Proof markers: every claim in prose names the evidence that makes it true.

roots.description: Directories to scan for Markdown. "." means the repository root, non-recursively.

maxDepth.description: How deep to descend below each root. Keeps a scan from wandering into a vendored tree.

mustCarryProof.description: Documents that must carry at least one marker in strict mode. Put the ones that make promises here.

commands.description: Marker prefix to the file that declares those commands, e.g. { "make": "Makefile", "task": "Taskfile.yml", "pnpm run": "package.json" }.

tracks.description: Handoff-driven development: the index of live work tracks and the handoffs it points at.

file.description: The index of live work tracks — one line per track, with a status and a next step.

log.description: Where a closed track's outcome is distilled.

specsDir.description: Where a lane's spec, tasks and handoff live, one directory per lane.

taskFile.description: The file inside a lane holding its task list, whose checked boxes the task gate reads.

gateTasks.description: Require a checked box in a live lane's task list to carry a proof marker.

queue.description: The work queue. State moves only through a passing verification, and CI re-runs every claim.

file.description: The queue itself: every item, its state, and the command that verifies it.

timeoutMinutes.description: A verification that runs longer than this is a failure with a stated cause, not a hang.

terminalByKind.description: Where an item lands when its verification passes, per kind.

locked.description: The files that define or enforce the acceptance signal, which an agent commit may not touch.

paths.description: Path prefixes. Empty means the check is off.

baseline.description: File naming the commit from which enforcement applies.

agentTrailer.description: The commit-message trailer that marks agent authorship.

coldStart.description: Can a fresh clone install and verify itself using nothing but the repository?

requiredFiles.description: Files a fresh clone must contain before anything is run — the ones the first command assumes.

entryDocs.description: Documents checked for paths that only resolve on one machine.

commands.description: The documented commands, run inside the fresh clone.

cleanExit.description: Clean state at session exit (lecture 12): no debris left behind, and progress written down.

scan.description: Path prefixes whose changed files are read. Empty means the check is off.

markers.description: Strings that pass a build and mean the work is unfinished. Null uses the defaults.

allow.description: Path fragments exempted — typically the files that name the markers themselves.

progressFile.description: The file a session must update when it changed code.

codePrefixes.description: What counts as code for the progress rule. Empty means anything that is not Markdown.

progressThreshold.description: Changed lines below which the progress rule stays quiet, so a one-line fix is not told to write a progress note. Defaults to 50.

requireCleanTree.description: Also fail when the working tree has uncommitted changes.

instructions.description: The instruction file kept a router rather than a manual (lecture 04).

release.description: The version is a claim made on several surfaces: they must agree.

manifest.description: Where the version being shipped is declared. Usually package.json.

changelog.description: The file describing each released version.

tagPrefix.description: What a tag for x.y.z looks like: "v" gives v1.2.3.
